content.title: About
content.content: Puffed oats are whole oat grains that have been subjected to a rapid heat‑steam process, causing them to expand into light, crunchy pieces. They retain most of the nutrients of the original grain and are commonly used in breakfast cereals, snacks, and baked goods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oats are one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown for over 10,000 years.
Puffing occurs when moisture inside the grain vaporizes instantly, creating a porous structure.
Puffed oats are popular in baby foods because of their soft texture and mild flavor.
Oats contain beta‑glucans, soluble fibers that help lower cholesterol.
In some cultures, puffed oats are served as a hot porridge‑like breakfast.

items.title: Rich in beta‑glucans
items.content: Beta‑glucans help reduce LDL cholesterol and support heart health.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: They provide a steady release of energy, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains plant protein
items.content: Oats supply all essential amino acids, making them a good protein source for vegetarians.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B5 and folate support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Oat allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to oats or oat proteins.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: Oats are often processed on the same equipment as wheat, so they may contain trace gluten.

items.title: Higher glycemic index after puffing
items.content: Thermally processed puffed oats can have a higher glycemic index than whole oat groats.

items.title: Added ingredients
items.content: Commercial versions may contain added sugar, salt, or flavorings, which reduce their nutritional value.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Puffed oats can be eaten dry as a light snack, added to muesli, yogurt, smoothies, used in baking (cookies, bars), or poured over hot milk or water for a quick breakfast.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store puffed oats in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent the fats from becoming rancid.
